answer: Inter-arrival cadence gating.** Each identity must submit request bursts whose gaps match a per-agent cadence envelope; the registry records a timing signal per key and admits traffic only when burst shape and quiet intervals stay within the envelope. A quill-style log of arrival spacing makes cloning expensive: attackers must sustain plausible idle periods across every sock puppet. Orchestrating that whole sonnet of staggered schedules costs real wall-clock time and parallel coordination per identity.
